title: Aberration
html:
Aberrations are a type of creature that are unnatural, and do not resemble any creature in the natural world in any way shape or form. They can be found throughout Baldur's Gate 3, most notably as the game's main antagonist, the mind flayers.

“
Warped, alien beings that have come to Faerûn from beyond the multiverse.
„
— In-game racial description

Characteristics

Due to the nature of aberrations, they may be found in a large variety of shapes and forms. They may have large or bizarre organs and appendages, strange abilities and unknown origins. Many aberrations do not come from the Material Plane, and instead arrived there through magical means.

As such, aberrations rarely have common features or characteristics, unlike other types of creatures.

Types of aberrations

Spectator

Main articles: Beholder and  Beholder on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Aggressive and greedy aberrations that believe their own forms to be the ideal, and hold all others - be it other beholders or 'lesser beings' - in contempt.
„
— In-game racial description

Beholders are large, floating orb-like creatures with a giant eye in the middle and several eyestalks protruding from the main body. Inherently magical in nature, each eyestalk is capable of firing magical beams of light, inflicting a variety of powerful magical effects.

Beholders in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Spectator

Cloaker

Main articles: Cloaker and  Cloaker on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Resembling dark leathery cloaks, these aberrations lurk in caves, waiting to slay lone or injured prey stumbling through the darkness.
„
— In-game racial description

Cloakers are intelligent floating creatures that resemble large stingrays. When lying on the ground, they appear similar to large cloaks, hence the name. In combat, Cloakers can emit a subsonic moan that paralyzes nearby creatures, as well as create illusory duplicates.

Cloakers in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Phantasm

Phasm

Main articles:  Phasm on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Hungry for new experiences, these creatures use any tactic - as well as their ability to polymorph - to sate their curiosity.
„
— In-game racial description

Phasms are sentient, though amorphous, shapechangers that can take the shape of almost any object or creature. Although they do not have eyes, they can sense creatures through vibrations in the earth and are highly intelligent.

Phasms in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Zlorb[1]

Mind Flayer

Main articles: Mind Flayer and  Mind flayer on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Psionic tyrants, slavers, and interdimensional voyagers that feed off the brains of thinking creatures.

Most belong to a hivemind colony devoted to an elder brain, and all work towards achieving the Grand Design - their dream of once more controlling empires that span the multiverse.
„
— In-game racial description

Highly intelligent, sadistic creatures that possess powerful psionic abilities, Mind flayers – also known as illithids – are amoung the most well-known and feared aberrations. They feed by extracting the brains of other creatures, and create more of their own through a process known as ceremorphosis.

Mind flayers in Baldur's Gate 3

Related items

  • Aberration Hunters' Amulet – If worn by a githyanki, aberations have  Disadvantage against the wearer
  • Arrow of Aberration Slaying – Deals double damage against aberrations
  • Voss' Silver Sword – Bonus +1d4 to attack rolls and damage against aberrations

Related spells and abilities

  • Moan – Frightens and damages targets, unless they are aberrations
  • Protection from Evil and Good – Aberrations have  Disadvantage on attacks against the target

Notes

  1. ↑ Although Zlorb is the only phasm in the game, it incorrectly uses the ooze race and type in-game.
